introduction: Follow the worried priest’s whip exchange and explore the mine’s engineering, planar intrusion, vault, industrial and worker-welfare stories.
orientation: Enter the mine from the rocky hillside and meet the worried priest in the barracks. Actual arrival discovers the zone; meeting the priest reveals his request.
Ask the priest about worried, worry or hi. These three aliases share one response about the order contacting an evil presence from a lower plane.

The priest accepts one exact balor’s whip for a badge of purity. The balor carries the equipped source whip in the Smouldering Pits of Misery. An exact supplied whip also fits; no remembered personal kill, greeting, first-source recovery or engineer investigation is required.

Carry the whip loose before offering it. The optional material row shows current loose custody; held, worn or contained material has different offering admission. It does not prove a personal source recovery or accepted history.

Offer the exact loose whip to the worried priest. One accepted exchange records completion. Spent materials, a missing badge, a source defeat or a room visit cannot replace or erase that receipt. The priest has no native departure clause.
The wall schematic warns against going down. Reading the map, discovering a route and surviving it are separate facts; a warning does not complete the priest’s request.

The engineer carries a hidden desk key. His locked desk contains a different key for the hub’s downward trapdoor. Source recovery, a supplied key, admitted unlocking, opening and crossing are separate outcomes.

The downward trapdoor has different keys on its two sides. Successful unlocking mirrors to the reciprocal side; builders must check reset, relocking and both directions before selecting a balanced repair.

The long shaft has no ground and can start an actual fall. Flight, levitation, mounts, climbing, movement refusal, landing and death must retain their native behavior; visiting the shaft does not prove survival.
Several lower pits use the fire sector and can schedule heat damage. The balor’s own room uses an indoor underground sector despite its flame description. Actual hazards follow the room controls.
The demon tunnel reaches openings into the food cellar and a hidden vault entrance. Discovering, opening and crossing those routes is distinct from ending an intrusion or restoring mine security.

The vault has a normal keyed entrance and a hidden tunnel entrance. Its two keyed faces have different pick protection. Builders must qualify actual lock admission while preserving intended access and challenge.

The vaultkeeper carries a vault key. Another key and a backpack are stocked in the random load grid, which has no declared route from the ordinary entrance. A reset declaration does not guarantee player access or renewed supply.

Vault chests and the rack are containers. The rack’s declared child is a golden boomerang; money-bag prose does not establish coins. Opening a container, recovering its child, admitted equipment use and donating recovered property are different outcomes.

The mine chief, cook, workers, rope puller, bellowman, miller, supervisor, driller, chiseller, cart pusher and janitors suggest wider upkeep and welfare stories. Builders must define real contributions, consent, beneficiaries, choice and lasting results; machinery and labor descriptions do not implement those outcomes.

New tracking requires active READY accounting. Daily replay remains disabled until actual source availability, exact input/reward/recipient/save/replay and accountable renewal are qualified. Wider planar, engineering, vault, industrial and welfare stories need real typed callers and explicit builder policy.
